title: Beyond Bias Scores: Unmasking Vacuous Neutrality in Small Language Models

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluated using multiple-choice question answering under ambiguous and disambiguated contexts to measure preferences for stereotypical versus anti-stereotypical answers (e.g., BBQ benchmark).
Evaluated using multiple-choice question answering and sentence completion tasks to detect stereotypical alignments against neutral or anti-stereotypical options (e.g., BBQ, StereoSet, CrowS-Pairs).
Evaluated through multiple-choice QA and sentence completion tasks comparing stereotypical and anti-stereotypical associations related to socioeconomic status.
Evaluated using multiple-choice QA and sentence completion tasks to measure the model's preference for stereotypical versus anti-stereotypical gender associations.
Evaluated through multiple-choice QA and sentence completions comparing stereotypical and anti-stereotypical associations regarding nationalities.
Evaluated using the BBQ benchmark by prompting models with multiple-choice questions about physical traits to detect stereotypical reasoning under ambiguous and disambiguated contexts.
Evaluated using multiple-choice QA and sentence completion tasks to measure alignment with racial and ethnic stereotypes, including intersectional categories (e.g., Race x Gender, Race x SES).
Evaluated through multiple-choice QA and sentence completion tasks to measure preferences for stereotypical versus anti-stereotypical associations regarding sexual orientation.
Evaluated using multiple-choice QA and sentence completion tasks comparing stereotypical and anti-stereotypical associations related to religious identities.

Evaluated by measuring the distribution of model predictions across multiple-choice answer positions (A, B, C) and computing normalized Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence against reference distributions to detect heuristic positional shortcuts.
